dimensions.form: PP or adjectival modifier naming a letter and its case (small/big/capital/uppercase/lowercase).
dimensions.meaning: Specifies orthographic case to disambiguate the sense or status of a label.
dimensions.function: Metalinguistic instruction about how a label should be written and interpreted.
dimensions.distribution: Adjunct to category labels; often parenthetical after the label.

1.definition: Specifies the capitalization of a letter in a label.
1.details: Capitalization can distinguish institutional and descriptive uses. Name conventions and ordinary spelling supply other uses. The capital-letter format can also emphatically present an example as fully deserving its label.

projection.target: With a capital R can distinguish the Romantic movement from a descriptive adjective. A quality with a capital letter can also express emphatic exemplarity. Neither the letter case nor the verbal specification determines noun subclass independently.
projection.evidence: The dictionary contrasts labels by written case and lists the emphatic idiom separately.

curious.title: Saying which letter case you mean
curious.summary: A phrase like with a small c tells the reader how a label is spelled and, with it, what it means.
curious.body:
Sometimes the letter at the start of a word changes what the word means. Catholic with a small c points to a non-institutional, descriptive sense. A big-D Democrat points to the party. The phrase naming the letter is a quick instruction about how to read the label.

Another use presents something as fully deserving a label. Saying a person is generous with a capital G suggests that the person fully deserves the label. The case of the letter doesn't decide by itself what kind of word the label is.
curious.try: Say the same label twice, once with a small first letter and once with a capital. Does the meaning change?

teacher.summary: Helps explain phrases like with a small c that tell the reader which sense of a label is meant.
teacher.explain: A PP or adjectival modifier names a letter and its case and attaches to a label. This dictionary treats it as a metalinguistic instruction: it tells the reader how to write or interpret the label, such as institutional versus descriptive. Name conventions and ordinary spelling supply other uses. The capital-letter format can also present an example as fully deserving its label, so a quality with a capital letter is emphatic. Neither letter case nor the specification fixes noun subclass by itself. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional and rests on dictionary entries.
teacher.terms: Related entries in this dictionary: common noun, proper name, proper noun.

contrasts.text: She's generous with a capital G.
contrasts.note: Emphatic, presenting her as fully deserving the label generous.

watch_for: A learner might take with a capital G as an instruction about spelling only, when it can also mean that the quality fully applies.
A learner might assume the capital letter by itself shows whether a word is a proper noun, when neither case nor the specification settles the noun subclass.
teacher.activity: Give students labels that have both an institutional and a descriptive sense. They write two sentences for each, using a phrase naming the letter case to show which sense they mean.
